provider: NSF ACCESS / Jetstream2 object store (OpenStack Swift, S3-compatible) — 1 TB default storage per allocation

free_tier.stated: By default, all allocations receive 1 TB (1000 GB) of Jetstream2 Storage quota.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: - **30 days from expiration:** If the allocation has not been renewed *(preferred)* or extended, all resources (instances, volumes, shares, images) on the allocation will be destroyed and *will not be recoverable.*

egress.terms: A temporary URL (or “temp URL”) is a signed, time-limited link that lets anyone download (`GET`) or upload (`PUT`) a single object without OpenStack credentials.

tooling: 'The Jetstream2 object store utilizes OpenStack Swift and is S3 compatible. You can utilize it via Horizon or the command line interface (CLI). From the CLI, you can use the OpenStack CLI's container and object commands, the AWS CLI's s3api, or other compatible tools.' Temp-URL keys give signed GET and signed PUT for a single object.
chaining: 1 TB default per allocation, but storage is credit-purchased, so the multiplier is ACCESS credits across project types (Explore 400k / Discover 1.5M / Accelerate 3M) and multiple requests (Explore and Discover explicitly allow 'Multiple requests allowed'). A 400k-credit Explore project = 400 GB above the default if spent purely on storage. The credit exchange rate, not a per-account cap, is the ceiling.

extras.quota_verbatim: 'By default, all allocations receive 1 TB (1000 GB) of Jetstream2 Storage quota.' Additional storage is bought with ACCESS credits at '1 ACCESS credit == 1 GB', and the default is a floor, not additive: 'the default 1 TB is replaced by a discrete allocation, not added on top of it.' Explore projects carry 400,000 credits; Discover 1,500,000; Accelerate 3,000,000 — so storage up to hundreds of TB is purchasable with credits, subject to justification review.
extras.limits_verbatim: per-object-cap: Swift, so large objects need segmentation; no single documented byte cap. Retention: storage is allocation-lifetime. request-rate: not published. Gate: ACCESS allocation (institutional email required; Explore is the lightest at 'Overview' requirements, reviewed but not a full panel).
extras.egress_verbatim: Unmetered within the NSF cloud; temp URLs and public containers serve objects over HTTPS.
extras.chaining_verbatim: 1 TB default per allocation, but storage is credit-purchased, so the multiplier is ACCESS credits across project types (Explore 400k / Discover 1.5M / Accelerate 3M) and multiple requests (Explore and Discover explicitly allow 'Multiple requests allowed'). A 400k-credit Explore project = 400 GB above the default if spent purely on storage — the credit exchange rate, not a per-account cap, is the ceiling.
extras.tooling_verbatim: 'The Jetstream2 object store utilizes OpenStack Swift and is S3 compatible. You can utilize it via Horizon or the command line interface (CLI). From the CLI, you can use the OpenStack CLI's container and object commands, the AWS CLI's s3api, or other compatible tools.' Temp-URL keys give signed GET and signed PUT for a single object.
extras.agent_focus: National and regional research-data infrastructure that hands out free (or grant-funded) bulk object storage to researchers: EUDAT/B2SHARE, EOSC EU Node, SURF, GÉANT ecosystem, NIRD/Sigma2, CSC Allas + LUMI-O, NAISS, DeiC, EuroHPC, DARIAH/CLARIN/ELIXIR nodes, NCI, ARDC Nectar, Digital Alliance of Canada, ACCESS/OSN, TACC, NCAR, NRP. Central question: which of these are SELF-SERVICE (anyone can get a login and a bucket) versus INSTITUTION-GATED (you need a university appointment, a national research affiliation, or a reviewed proposal). The per-project quotas here are the largest numbers in the whole survey — 10-150 TB — so the gate, not the quota, is the finding.

binding_note: the write is a queue with a person or a rule in it, so the upload rate is set by somebody else
